correctness.rationale: For every \(r\ge2\) and \(n\ge4r+3\), the integer pair-extension lemma proves all four third-vertex adjacency conditions, including endpoint exceptions and repetitions. Its exhaustive five-row pointed-profile table gives a symmetric three-round EF response. A rank-three two-vertex domination formula separates \(n=4r+2\) from the tail, and a neighborhood-containment formula separates the tail from cycle powers. The least-order representative is checked with full three-round recursion for every smaller noncomplete path-power parameter pair (36 cases), not by sampling. Two independently implemented neighborhood checkers corroborate 89,205 and 105,200 pair cases; replay matches included outputs. The infinite proof rests on interval inequalities rather than the finite tests.

originality.rationale: The theorem is a cross-radius first-order three-round equivalence theorem about powers of undirected paths with five pointed boundary regimes, not merely ordinary paths, cyclic powers, first-order model-checking complexity, interval-representation preservation, or identification via counting logic. Full primary texts on ordinary paths/cycles, interval-graph logical model checking and interval-graph powers were materially inspected. Indexed record searches and accessible prior claims yielded no equivalent statement. This is a best-knowledge originality determination subject to unindexed-history risk.

value.rationale: Path powers are canonical proper/unit interval graphs. A sharp two-parameter logical stabilization theorem with five exactly characterized boundary pointed profiles has structural value independent of finite enumeration: it gives a common rank-three theory across unbounded graph orders, radii and degrees, exhibits the exact last missing order \(4r+2\), provides an eleven-vertex least representative, and separates superficially similar cycle-power tails.
